_comment: Annotated example for poll_connector.py --config, targeting IBM QRadar's own REST API Offense-listing endpoint -- a plain GET with a static 'SEC' header token, which fits PollerConfig directly with no OAuth2 or multi-step choreography needed. Point base_url at YOUR QRadar console's REST API and adjust the fields filter to your own QRadar version's schema. Delete this _comment field (or leave it; it's ignored) before using.
name: qradar-offenses
_comment_auth: Create an authorized service in the QRadar console (Admin -> Authorized Services) to get a SEC token -- QRadar's REST API expects it in a header literally named 'SEC', not 'Authorization: Bearer'. auth_token_env names an ENVIRONMENT VARIABLE holding the real token; never put the token itself in this file.
_comment_query: fields narrows the response to what normalize_qradar() actually uses; filter restricts to open offenses only (adjust or drop for your own triage workflow). sort ascending by id keeps the cursor moving forward through a large backlog.
_comment_records_path: QRadar's /api/siem/offenses response body is already a bare JSON array of offense objects -- no wrapper key to unwrap, so records_path is left unset.
_comment_cursor: QRadar's AQL-style filter is a single expression under one 'filter' query param -- PollerConfig's cursor_query_param would need to *merge* an 'id>N' clause into that same already-used 'filter' key rather than replace it wholesale, which the generic connector's model can't do. cursor_query_param/cursor_field are deliberately left unset here, same as the Elastic example config; Cavendex's own dedup (keyed on each offense's real id via normalize_qradar()'s dedup_key) absorbs the resulting re-fetch of already-seen offenses on every poll instead.
_comment_normalizer: Uses the real QRadar Offense normalizer (ingestion/normalizers.py:normalize_qradar) instead of a generic field_map -- it understands magnitude's 0-10 composite scale and offense_source's ambiguous IP-or-username-or-hostname shape, neither of which a flat field_map alone can do.
